name: Aether
one_liner: Launch, track and steer the coding agents on your own Aether server: see what needs you, read runs and pull requests, and act.
description:
Aether is self-hosted software that runs coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and opencode in containers on your own server. This connector links Claude to the Aether server you are a member of, through the Aether edge at edge.onaether.dev.

Ask what needs you, what your agents did this week, or what a run changed. Read a run's conversation or terminal, its reports, diff, and its pull request's checks, reviews and comments. Search runs and a workspace's team memory, and see which active runs touch the same files.

With the Launch and message scope, checked by default on the consent page, launch a run on a task, message a run, answer an agent's question, pause or resume a run, and accept a run's reported success. With the Stop and approve scope, off by default, allow or deny one permission request, stop or close a run.

Who it is for: developers whose team already runs an Aether server. You need an Aether account on a server linked to the Aether edge, signed in with GitHub.

Limitations: agents run with the access your server gave them, so a launched agent can push branches and open pull requests. No connector tool installs Aether, changes server settings, merges pull requests or deletes repositories or workspaces; an agent you instruct can do what its credentials allow. Text written by agents, teammates and GitHub users is returned as untrusted data.

prerequisites: An Aether account on an Aether server linked to edge.onaether.dev, with a GitHub account bound to your member. A server under edge-access approved-devices also asks for a one-time code from aether mcp.
use_cases: Triage: ask what needs you across your runs (agent questions, permission requests, runs awaiting review) and answer from the chat.
Delegate: launch a run on a task in a workspace, then follow its state and reports.
Review: read what a run changed, its pull request's checks and reviewers' comments, and accept or redirect the work.
Coordinate: see which active runs touch the same files and message a run to change course.
example_prompts: Launch a Claude Code run in the api workspace to fix the flaky login test.
Is CI green on the login fix pull request? What did reviewers say?
Which runs touch the same files as the migration run?
Tell the parser run to use the new tokenizer.

data_handling.api_ownership: First-party: every tool calls the Aether server the user connected, through the Aether edge that 3xDevOps operates.
